findings.F1: Sense 1 collocations list the untypical 'tall fabric'.
findings.F2: The sense 1 false-friends adaptation note names Spanish and Portuguese instead of being language-neutral.
findings.F3: The sense 1 definition uses technical words (interlacing, filaments, warp and weft) beyond a B1 learner.
findings.F4: The 'fabric is not a factory' fact is stated in four fields (usage note, learner error, sense and entry adaptation notes).
findings.F5: The sense 1 definition is too narrow: it describes only woven cloth, excluding knitted and nonwoven fabric.
findings.F6: The fabric/cloth rule of choice sits in usage_note instead of synonym_discrimination.
findings.F7: Sense 2 merges the figurative society structure with the literal (mainly British) building structure.
findings.F8: The core idea's 'from that' makes a wrong derivation claim (the building sense is older), and origin claims belong only in etymology.
